idiom_name: ox supervised { fork {} + f.join() } over JDK 21+ virtual threads
implementation_notes: Scala's standard library Future is unstructured (no scope, no cancellation), so structured concurrency comes from libraries: ox's supervised block runs forks that the block cannot outlive - on block exit running forks are interrupted and the block returns only after all of them have finished, and a failing fork cancels the scope (forking outside supervised is a compile-time error). Effect libraries express the same with scoped fibers (ZIO scopes, cats-effect parTupled with cancellation). Without such a library, Future.traverse/sequence joins but cancellation remains impossible.
pitfalls: Futures cannot be interrupted, so cancellation in Scala requires interruption-aware code (virtual threads via ox); Future-based scopes leak work.
The global ExecutionContext is a ForkJoinPool sized to the available processors; blocking work must use blocking {} or a dedicated pool.
forkUnsupervised escapes the scope's supervision by design - use it only when the escaped lifetime is intentionally owned elsewhere.
